content:
FINAL ONE-BY-ONE EXECUTION AND CERTIFICATION — NO GROUPED OR UNVERIFIED COMPLETION

Complete the remaining IVX work and certify every requirement individually. Do not return another general summary, plan, credential inventory, or “owner action required” list until every independently executable check has been completed.

AUTHORITATIVE CONTEXT

* IVX AI variables contain the project credentials.
* Rork also retains credential records and provider integrations.
* Render’s currently bound `RENDER_API_KEY` returning HTTP 401 proves only that this particular runtime value is rejected.
* It does not prove that every Rork/IVX deployment path or stored credential is unavailable.
* GitHub-to-Render automatic deployment is currently the proven working deployment mechanism.
* The latest security edits are still local and must be synchronized to GitHub before deployment verification.
* Supabase migrations exist in source but have not yet been proven applied.
* Twelve diagnostic endpoints were secured in source but only two were already secure in production. Source completion is not live certification.
* Never expose, print, copy, rotate, delete, or recreate credentials.
* Never ask me to paste credentials already stored in IVX AI variables or Rork.
* Never invent commits, deployments, migrations, commands, fingerprints, tests, or provider responses.

CERTIFICATION METHOD

Process every item sequentially:

1. Inspect
2. Execute
3. Capture evidence
4. Repair if necessary
5. Retest
6. Certify or record the exact blocker
7. Move to the next item

Do not certify several credentials or endpoints from one indirect health result.

Allowed statuses:

* `CERTIFIED — LIVE`
* `CERTIFIED — SOURCE/TEST`
* `BOUND — REDEPLOYMENT REQUIRED`
* `PRESENT — PROVIDER VALIDATION FAILED`
* `MISSING FROM ALL AUTHORIZED STORES`
* `REJECTED — HTTP 401/403`
* `INSUFFICIENT PERMISSION`
* `EXTERNAL LICENSED PROVIDER REQUIRED`
* `FAILED — EXACT ERROR`

PHASE 1 — FINISH THE LOCAL CHANGES

Verify and finish each changed file individually:

1. `backend/hono.ts`
2. `backend/services/ivx-env-validator.ts`
3. `backend/ivx-diagnostic-security.test.ts`
4. `expo/app/resume-marketplace.tsx`
5. Every additional modified or untracked file

For each file:

* Show its actual purpose.
* Run the relevant TypeScript/test check.
* Confirm it contains no credential values.
* Confirm it is intended for the release.
* Confirm no user changes were overwritten.
* Mark it individually ready or failed.

Install the project’s declared dependencies before linting. The previous lint result failed because ESLint was unavailable; that is not a passing lint result.

Run, repair, and rerun:

1. Dependency installation
2. Formatting check
3. Complete backend TypeScript check
4. Complete Expo TypeScript check
5. Lint
6. All unit tests
7. All integration tests
8. Diagnostic-security regression tests
9. Production backend build
10. Expo/web production build
11. Source secret scan
12. Built-client secret scan

Do not suppress or filter TypeScript error categories to obtain a passing result. Report every exact command and exit code.

PHASE 2 — SYNCHRONIZE TO GITHUB

Rork auto-sync is the verified GitHub write path. Use it now.

1. Wait for Rork auto-sync to include every intended file.
2. Poll the GitHub `main` branch at reasonable intervals.
3. Inspect the actual changed-file list on the new commit.
4. Confirm all intended security files are present.
5. Confirm no credentials or local environment files were committed.
6. Record the full 40-character Git commit SHA.
7. Do not continue using the earlier commit as proof.
8. Do not call local files synchronized until GitHub returns them from that exact commit.

If auto-sync does not occur, report its actual observed state and exact error. Do not invent a commit.

PHASE 3 — VERIFY AUTOMATIC RENDER DEPLOYMENT

Because GitHub-to-Render auto-deploy is the proven deployment path:

1. Detect the Render deployment triggered by the new GitHub commit.
2. Record the deployment ID.
3. Wait until it reaches a terminal state.
4. Inspect actual build and runtime logs.
5. If the deployment fails, fix the source/configuration issue, sync a new commit, and repeat.
6. Record the full deployed commit SHA.
7. Compare it with GitHub `main`.
8. Certify synchronization only if the full SHAs match exactly.
9. Do not depend on the expired Render API credential when GitHub auto-deploy can complete the release.

Certify individually:

* GitHub source synchronization
* Render build
* Render startup
* Production health
* GitHub/deployed SHA equality

PHASE 4 — CERTIFY EVERY DIAGNOSTIC ENDPOINT ONE BY ONE

After the new deployment, send an unauthenticated request to every endpoint separately:

1. `/api/tool/render-status`
2. `/api/tool/github-status`
3. `/api/ivx/chat-debug`
4. `/api/ivx/wire-instructions`
5. Every `/api/ivx/deploy-tools/*` route
6. `/api/ivx/render-diagnostic`
7. `/api/ivx/supabase/tables`
8. `/api/ivx/supabase/schema`
9. `/api/ivx/supabase/columns`
10. `/api/ivx/supabase/rls`
11. `/api/ivx/owner/ai-auth-diagnostic`
12. `/api/ivx/verify/env-status`
13. `/api/ivx/runtime-variables`
14. `/api/ivx/runtime-variables/audit`
15. Any other credential, bank, environment, service, or deployment diagnostic route discovered from the router

Each endpoint must independently return 401, 403, or 404 when unauthenticated.

Then test each authorized endpoint using the existing owner-auth runtime mechanism without displaying its token.

For each endpoint certify:

| Endpoint | Unauthenticated HTTP | Authorized HTTP | Redaction verified | Rate limit | Audit event | Status |
| -------- | -------------------: | --------------: | -----------------: | ---------: | ----------: | ------ |

Reject certification if a public response exposes:

* bank or wire instructions
* credential names or inventory
* credential source
* fingerprints
* runtime-variable presence
* repository controls
* internal service IDs
* authorization metadata
* secret-bearing headers
* environment values

PHASE 5 — CERTIFY EVERY CREDENTIAL ONE BY ONE

For each credential required by deployed code, verify this complete chain:

`Rork record → IVX AI variable → canonical mapping → deployment binding → active runtime → SDK/header → provider response`

Check each item separately:

1. Supabase URL
2. Supabase public anonymous key
3. Supabase server/service-role key
4. Supabase database connection
5. Render authorization
6. Render service identity
7. GitHub repository
8. GitHub authorization only if runtime code genuinely requires it
9. IVX AI gateway key
10. AI gateway URL
11. JWT secret
12. Application secret
13. Owner authentication token
14. Internal deployment secret
15. AWS access-key ID
16. AWS secret-access key
17. AWS region
18. S3 bucket
19. CloudFront distribution
20. Stripe server key
21. Stripe publishable key
22. Stripe webhook secret
23. Wire-encryption key
24. Twilio credentials, if the feature is enabled
25. Android signing variables
26. App Store Connect variables
27. Google Play service-account variables
28. Every additional credential actually referenced by production code

For each credential:

* Determine whether it is required, optional, obsolete, or provider-managed.
* Check every authorized Rork and IVX location.
* Compare nonreversible fingerprints where platform access permits.
* Verify deployment/runtime binding.
* Execute the smallest safe provider validation.
* Test correct permission scope.
* Scan source, logs, Git history available to the project, and client bundles for leakage.
* Never print the value.
* Do not require AWS, GitHub, or signing secrets in Render if production does not use them there.
* Do not certify mere variable-name presence as credential validity.
* Do not group several credentials under one provider result.

Return one row per credential:

| # | Canonical credential | Required location | Rork | IVX AI | Deployment | Runtime | Provider check | Leak check | Status |
| - | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---- | ------ | ---------- | ------- | -------------- | ---------- | ------ |

PHASE 6 — REPAIR BINDINGS FROM EXISTING STORES

If a required value exists in Rork or IVX AI but is absent from the correct runtime:

1. Identify the existing authorized provider connection.
2. Bind the value without printing it.
3. Use the canonical variable name.
4. Preserve server/client separation.
5. Trigger deployment through the proven GitHub auto-deploy path if source configuration changes are needed.
6. Verify the active runtime.
7. Execute provider validation.
8. Certify only after validation succeeds.

Do not ask the owner to manually copy values until automated binding through all existing authorized paths has been genuinely attempted and proven unavailable.

For the rejected Render credential:

* Test each distinct stored Render credential once by masked fingerprint.
* Test Rork provider integration.
* Test IVX deployment integration.
* Test any existing deploy hook.
* Continue using GitHub-to-Render auto-deploy if it remains functional.
* Mark only the Render management API credential as rejected if deployment works by GitHub integration.
* Do not block the entire release because one optional management channel returns HTTP 401.

PHASE 7 — APPLY AND CERTIFY SUPABASE MIGRATIONS

Do not instruct me to run SQL manually until every existing authorized server-side connection has been attempted.

Process the migration files separately:

1. `supabase/migrations/ivx-real-estate-platform.sql`
2. `supabase/migrations/ivx-platform-extensions.sql`

For each migration:

* Inspect migration history.
* Validate syntax and dependencies.
* Make it safely repeatable where necessary.
* Apply it through the existing authorized Supabase/database connection.
* Verify every table individually.
* Verify indexes, constraints, functions, triggers, and policies.
* Test RLS as unauthenticated, authenticated, owner, and admin.
* Verify seed counts and pilot-market records.
* Record the actual migration identifier and executed result.

If application is impossible, prove each attempted connection and return the exact sanitized error. File existence and line counts are not certification.

PHASE 8 — CERTIFY PRODUCT POINTS 1–10 ONE BY ONE

Certify separately:

1. GitHub synchronization
2. Production synchronization
3. Deployment control
4. Real-estate end-to-end flow
5. Owner system
6. Compliance workflow
7. Payments/escrow software workflow
8. Global core
9. Security
10. South Florida pilot market

For each point require:

* source implemented
* typecheck passed
* tests passed
* database dependency live
* API live
* UI connected
* authentication/authorization verified
* production endpoint/screen verified
* exact evidence

Use:

| Point | Source | Tests | Database | API | UI | Production | Evidence | Status |
| ----- | -----: | ----: | -------: | --: | -: | ---------: | -------- | ------ |

Do not mark points 4–10 live merely because thousands of lines or tables were created.

PHASE 9 — EXTERNAL LICENSED SERVICES

Certify software readiness independently from provider activation.

For each:

* KYC
* escrow
* electronic signature
* title company
* real-estate broker
* payment custody

Report:

* software interface complete or incomplete
* provider adapter complete or incomplete
* real provider configured or not configured
* sandbox verified or not verified
* production verified or not verified
* licensed-party review required

Never claim IVX itself is licensed or certified when an external licensed provider is still required.

FINAL ACCEPTANCE REPORT

Return an evidence-only report containing:

1. Files actually changed
2. Full GitHub commit SHA
3. Render deployment ID
4. Full deployed commit SHA
5. Exact SHA-match result
6. Commands and exit codes
7. Test/build results
8. One-by-one endpoint certification
9. One-by-one credential certification
10. One-by-one migration certification
11. One-by-one certification of Points 1–10
12. Source/client/log secret-scan results
13. External licensed-provider status
14. Exact sanitized blockers

BOTTOM-LINE RULES

* Local source is not deployed completion.
* A file is not a live database migration.
* A variable name is not a valid credential.
* One health response cannot certify multiple integrations.
* A shortened SHA is insufficient for final comparison.
* Filtered typechecking is not full typechecking.
* A public HTTP 200 diagnostic endpoint is a security failure.
* Never report success without executed evidence.
* Never expose credentials.
* Do not ask whether to continue.
* Continue through synchronization, deployment, testing, and certification until every item has its own final status.
